artifacts.summary: Narrowed orchestrate-batch-admit.sh's in_batch deferral rule to compare a candidate only against peers already admitted this cycle; added a regression suite reproducing the observed A/C/D wasted-cycle chain; brought the schema doc and header comment into sync; full gate run clean of any batch-admit-related failure.

completion_data.completion_summary: Converted orchestrate-batch-admit.sh's in_batch collision jq generator into a reduce over ascending-project_number-sorted candidates threading a running admitted-set lookup, so a lower-numbered peer only blocks a candidate when that peer itself admits this cycle; added a new regression suite (test-orchestrate-batch-admit.sh, 3 cases) and updated batch-admit-schema.md plus the script's header comment to match.

memory_candidates.content: When converting an order-independent jq top-level generator (`$cands[] as $c | ...`) into a sequential admitted-set-aware fold, use `reduce ($cands | sort)[] as $c ({results: {}}; ...)` to compute decisions in a required dependency order, but re-emit output by iterating the ORIGINAL (unsorted) input array against the fold's `.results` map -- this decouples decision order from emission order and preserves any caller-argument-order output contract without re-sorting the emission pass.
